info.title: Paduraksa admin API
info.description: The REST API of the Paduraksa admin app. Authenticate with an API token (Authorization: Bearer ...) or a signed-in session. Paths are kebab-case; JSON members are camelCase; IDs are typed strings (host_...); times are ISO 8601 in UTC; enums are strings. A create is POST to the collection: 201 with Location and the created object. A change is PUT or PATCH: 200 with the object. A delete is 204. Every collection takes limit and cursor and answers { items, nextCursor }. Every error is RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a traceId. Config objects (hosts, routes, upstreams, profiles, the settings, ...) and rollbacks take optimistic concurrency: a read carries an ETag (an object's version, or the latest revision's ID), and a change sends it back as one quoted tag in If-Match. Without it the answer is 428; a stale or weak tag is 412 (the problem's conflict says what is current); an unquoted tag, a list or '*' is 400. Creating with POST needs none, and neither do the objects that carry no version (certificates, ACME accounts, DNS providers, notification channels, users). Changes to config objects also take ?dryRun=true, which returns the plan and commits nothing. A change that was stored but could not go live is 500 with code config.publishFailed, the stored revision and the new ETag. Each operation names the permission it needs (x-required-permission).

The body is YAML (application/yaml), at most 4 MiB. The mode says whether what the YAML leaves out is kept or deleted. Objects are matched by id, else by name (a host by its first host name). Requires the `config:write` permission.

post.description:
Streams one archive (application/octet-stream, .pdkbak) holding the config database, the vault database and the last-known-good config, all encrypted under the passphrase in the body (at least 12 characters) with AES-256-GCM and an Argon2id key. The vault's keys in it are wrapped under a key made for this archive, so it restores on another machine with that machine's own master key, and it is useless without the passphrase, which nothing can recover. The server keeps running and the databases are read consistently. Making one takes about a second of CPU and 64 MiB; one at a time (a second request while one runs gets 409). The passphrase goes in the JSON body over the admin's HTTPS, never in a URL.

Requires the `backup:create` permission.

post.description:
Replays the entries on the latest revision and dry-runs them as one change: the diff, the compiler's warnings, the admin lock-out guard (?force=true overrides it) and the errors of the whole set. The answer's reviewToken (also its ETag) is what apply must send back as If-Match to commit exactly this: it covers what the draft would do, so a change to the draft, to an object it writes or refers to, or to what the compiler says about it makes it stale, while an unrelated commit does not. realm.description: The realm of the password prompt: 1-64 printable ASCII characters; null = the list's name.

The users and their realm; null = no password.

satisfy.description:
AccessListSatisfy.All (built-in): the address must pass and then, when the list has
        users, the credentials. AccessListSatisfy.Any: either passes, so an address in the allow list needs no
        password. A denied address is refused either way.

passCredentialsUpstream.description:
Forward the `Authorization` header to the upstream. Off: the proxy's
            credentials are removed once the list has accepted them, because the upstream has no use for them.

AccessListConfig.description:
A named set of rules that hosts and routes apply to who may reach them: IP allow and deny entries, and HTTP basic-auth
users, combined as AccessListSatisfy AccessListConfig.Satisfy says. It is a top-level object, so one list can guard several hosts and
routes, and it replaces the inline IP allow list the settings used to carry.

addressRefused.description: Requests refused for their address (403, or dropped).

unauthorized.description: Requests answered 401: no credentials, or wrong ones.

cacheHits.description: Passwords accepted from the five-minute memory, without a check.

queued.description: Requests that waited for a password check to come free.

queueFull.description: Requests refused with 429 at once: the line was full, or their client already had its share of it.

queueTimeouts.description: Requests refused with 429 after waiting the maximum.

AccessListCountries.description:
The country rules of an access list. The country is the one Cloudflare reports in `CF-IPCountry`, so they only
            apply in a Cloudflare trusted-proxy mode; elsewhere every request's country is unknown (the config warns:
            `accessList.countries.noSource`). Codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`DE`, upper case in a stored document) plus
            `T1` (Tor exit nodes) and `XX` (country unknown).

AccessListId.description: An access list: IP allow and deny entries and basic-auth users, which hosts and routes name.

dropDenied.description: Abort a refused connection instead of answering 403.

oneOf.description: The country rules; null = none.

AccessListIp.description:
The address rules of an access list. Deny wins over allow; an empty allow list means any address that isn't
            denied, and a non-empty one means only those. The countries are part of the same rules: a request must pass every allow list
            that has entries and match no deny list.

oneOf.description: The list those routes apply; absent when they are not guarded.

AccessListOverride.description: Routes guarded by another access list, or none.

overrides.description: The routes that differ from the host's list, grouped by what guards them instead.

oneOf.description: The list the host names; absent when it names none.

users.description: How many users it asks a password of; 0 means addresses only.

addressRanges.description: The address ranges its allow and deny entries cover, after merging overlaps.

countries.description: The countries (and Tor or unknown) its allow and deny lists name.

AccessListRef.description: A named access list, with what it asks of a visitor.

enabled.description: Apply the resolved list. Built-in default: on. Off lifts an inherited list.

oneOf.description: The list to apply; null = inherit. With bool? AccessListSettings.Enabled off the reference is kept but inert.

AccessListSettings.description:
Which access list a layer applies. AccessListId? AccessListSettings.AccessListId names a list the document declares; both fields
            inherit on their own, so a host can turn an inherited list off without forgetting which one it was, and a route can
            inherit its host's, name another, or turn it off. A layer that names a list without stating
            bool? AccessListSettings.Enabled leaves the switch to the built-in default, which is on.

username.description: 1-64 visible ASCII characters, no colon, case-sensitive.

credentialId.description:
The vault's handle on this user's password. The server makes it when a user is first written with a
            Password and keeps it when the password changes, so a rollback restores the user but not an older password.
            A user whose credential the vault doesn't hold (deleted since, or never set) can't sign in, and the config says so in a warning
            (`accessList.user.noPassword`). A write that names a user already on the list and sends neither a password nor an ID keeps
            the credential the list has.

password.description:
Write-only: the plain password of a new or changed user, 1-256 bytes in UTF-8. The server hands it to the
            vault before anything is validated, stored or audited and never returns it, so it is null in every document it hands out.

AccessListUserConfig.description:
One basic-auth user. The document names the user's password in the vault and never holds it, or anything that
            verifies it: no read returns a password or a hash.

AcmeAccountId.description: An ACME account. Its account key lives in the vault under this ID.

AcmeAccountStatus.description: The state of an ACME account row. Persisted by name (ModelNames).

AcmeAccountSummary.description:
An ACME account as listed. No key material and no vault reference: the account key and the external-account-binding secret stay in the
vault, named only by the internal row.

AcmeChallengeType.description: The ACME challenge type a certificate's names are proven with. Persisted by name (ModelNames), the same as in RFC 8555.

AcmeOrderId.description: An ACME order, i.e. one issuance or renewal attempt for a certificate.

AcmeOrderStatus.description:
Where an ACME order stands in Paduraksa's own bookkeeping. The CA's order is the authority on what
            happens next, so a resume re-reads it; this status is for operators and for the scheduler to see what is
            unfinished.

count.description: How many requests (or, for the largest responses, how many bytes).

error.description: The most Count may overshoot by; 0 when exact.

AnalyticsCount.description:
A label and how many times it was seen, for a table or a distribution. Error is how far Count may be
above the truth when the table comes from a sketch (top paths, referers, user agents, largest responses): the true count is at least
`Count - Error` and at most `Count`. It is 0 for a count that is exact.

stepSeconds.description: The usual width of one Series step: 5 minutes for the hour, 1 hour for the day, 3 hours for the week and 1 day for the month.

statusClasses.description: Requests by status class: `none` (no response), `1xx` to `5xx`. Exact.

statuses.description: The most common exact status codes. Exact up to 64 distinct codes a bucket.

methods.description: Requests by method. Exact up to 16 distinct methods a bucket.

protocols.description: Requests by HTTP version: `HTTP/1.0`, `HTTP/1.1`, `HTTP/2`, `HTTP/3`, `other`. Exact. (The TLS version is not available to the analytics without work on the request path.)

topReferers.description: Where requests came from: `direct`, `(same site)` and referers reduced to scheme and host.

topUserAgents.description: The most common raw user agents.

slowestPaths.description: Paths with the highest 95th-percentile time among the tracked ones with at least five requests.

largestResponses.description: Paths by the bytes of their declared responses (the count is bytes).

browsers.description: Browser families of the clients that are not bots.

browserVersions.description: Browser families with their major version, for the clients that are not bots.

operatingSystems.description: Operating system families of the clients that are not bots.

topBots.description: The most active bots by name.

visitors.description: Estimated unique visitors over the whole range, the union of the steps' and not their sum (about 1.6 % standard error). A visitor active across a restart counts once on each side of it.

botRequests.description: Requests whose user agent is an automated client.

coveredSeconds.description: How many seconds of the range the server was running for.

warnings.description: What compiles but probably isn't intended.

An error answer of the REST API: an RFC 9457 problem details object (`application/problem+json`). Every error
the admin app answers under `/api` has this shape, whoever produced it: `type`, `title`, `status`,

scopes.description: What it may do: a subset of what its owner may do.

ConfigDocument.description:
The whole proxy config: global settings, profiles, upstreams, rate-limit policies, access lists and hosts with their routes. It is the
source of truth: each revision stores it as canonical JSON (ConfigJsonContext), and startup, rollback,
diff and YAML export all read it. It holds references only, never secrets.

version.description: Changes with every change to the draft; apply names the one it reviewed (`If-Match`).

updatedAt.description: When it was last changed; 30 days later (ExpiresAt) an untouched draft is dropped.

expiresAt.description: When it is dropped if nobody touches it.

entries.description: The entries in the order they were added, each with its state against the head.

The latest revision now; null while there is none.

JSON pointer (RFC 6901) into the document, e.g. `/hosts/3/routes/0/path`; `""` is the
            whole document. Indices count in the document as validated: as the client sent it, before canonicalisation;
            validation and compile errors both point at what the client wrote, and an object command's errors are relative to
            the object it sent.

ConfigWarning.description:
Something about a config that compiles but probably isn't what the admin wants: a host without a certificate that
covers it, a binding to a certificate that expired. Surfaced next to the result (the dashboard's "hosts without
coverage"), never blocks a change on its own.

maxPerIp.description: Open connections one client address may hold; 0 means the limit is off. Trusted proxies are exempt.

denyListRefused.description: Connections refused for being in the deny list.

limitRefused.description: Connections refused because their address already held the limit.

uncounted.description: Connections let through uncounted because the table had no entry for their address; 0 unless a flood from many addresses filled it.

oneOf.description: The access list whose deny addresses are refused before TLS; absent when none is named.

ConnectionCounters.description: The connection stage: what runs before the TLS handshake and what it has refused over the range, over TCP and QUIC.

addressRanges.description: The deny address ranges it covers, after merging overlaps.

maxConnectionsPerIp.description:
Open connections one client address may hold (an IPv6 /64 counts as one address), 0 to
            100000; 0 turns the cap off. Null = the built-in 256. Over it a connection is closed at once, before TLS.

denyListId.description:
The access list whose `ip.deny` addresses are refused before TLS, trusted proxies
            included. Only its deny addresses apply here: its allow addresses, countries and users are request rules. Null = none.

ConnectionSettings.description:
What the proxy does with a connection before the TLS handshake (docs/design/hot-path.md "A. Connection"). Global only: a connection has no host yet.
A visitor behind a trusted proxy (Cloudflare, a load balancer) shares the proxy's address here, so the proxy is exempt from
the cap and its visitors are judged by their real addresses later, at the gate.

mode.description: How the page is written. Default: ErrorPageMode.Message.

heading.description: ErrorPageMode.Message only: the heading, 1 to 120 characters on one line. It is also the page's title.

text.description: ErrorPageMode.Message only: the sentence under the heading, up to 500 characters on one line; may be empty.

ErrorPageContent.description:
One error page: a heading and a sentence rendered into Paduraksa's own layout, or the operator's whole document. The
text may use the variables `{status}`, `{statusText}`, `{requestId}`, `{host}` and `{cfRay}`
(ErrorPageText); `{{` writes a literal brace.

ErrorPageMode.description: How an operator's error page is written.

html.description: The page's document, which a client shows in a sandboxed frame without scripts.

contentSecurityPolicy.description: The `Content-Security-Policy` the proxy serves it with.

ErrorPagePreview.description: A page rendered the way the proxy serves it, with sample values (`{requestId}`, `{host}`, `{cfRay}`).

page.description: The page, as it would be stored.

status.description:
The status it is served with, 100 to 599; its `{status}` and `{statusText}` say it. For a page of one of the
            statuses that is the status itself, for the maintenance page the status the host answers maintenance with.

maintenance.description: The page is a maintenance page, which a host may serve with another status than an error page's.

ErrorPagePreviewRequest.description: A page to preview: the page as written and the status it would be served with.

ErrorPageSource.description: Which layer of the settings chain an error page came from.

oneOf.description: 403: an access list, rule set or Cloudflare check refused the request.
404: no route takes the path, or the host is unknown.
413: the request body is over the host's or route's limit.
414: the request target is over the host's limit.
421: the connection can't be used for the host (a client that coalesced it must retry on its own).
429: a rate limit, or a queue of password checks, turned the request away.
431: the request has more headers, or bigger ones, than the host takes.
502: the upstream, or a sign-in service, didn't answer properly.
503: no healthy destination, or a sign-in service is busy.
504: the upstream, or a sign-in service, took too long.
The page a host in maintenance answers with (MaintenanceSettings).

Answer with the page above when the upstream's own response is an error with a page here (the statuses of this
record), decided from the status and content type when the response starts: the upstream's body is discarded unread. Never for
an upgrade, an event stream or gRPC. Built-in default: UpstreamErrorReplacement.Off.

ErrorPagesSettings.description:
The pages a host answers with in place of the built-in ones, one entry per status the gate and the upstream can answer
with a page, and whether an upstream's own error bodies are replaced by them. Each entry inherits on its own and is
replaced whole by a layer that sets it (a heading from one layer and a document from another make no page). A status with
no entry in any layer is served from the built-in page.

url.description:
The endpoint, an absolute `http` or `https` URL with no credentials. For a preset the bare address
            (`http://authelia:9091`) is enough: the preset's path is added when the URL has none.

preset.description: Which provider this is; null is ForwardAuthPreset.Custom.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the answer; null = int ForwardAuthLimits.DefaultTimeoutSeconds. A timeout refuses the request (504).

cacheSeconds.description:
How long an allow is remembered; null = int ForwardAuthLimits.DefaultCacheSeconds, 0 = never. A session the provider has
            revoked still works for that long.

cacheScope.description:
What a remembered allow covers; null = the preset's. `host` reuses an allow for every path only when the provider named
            someone (copied an identity header); an allow without one is remembered for its own method and path.

requestHeaders.description:
Client headers sent to the endpoint besides the standard ones (cookies, authorization, user agent, accept and the
            `X-Forwarded-*` set); null = none.

responseHeaders.description:
The endpoint's response headers copied to the upstream when it allows a request, and removed from the client's own
            request first. A trailing `*` makes a name a prefix. Null = the preset's; an empty list = none. `Authorization`, `Cookie` and
            `Proxy-Authorization` can't be listed: the client's own are forwarded as they were.

oneOf.description: Where a browser without a session is sent when the endpoint answers 401; null = the preset's. Without one the 401 is relayed as it is.

ForwardAuthConfig.description:
A forward-auth endpoint. For each request the proxy asks it with a `GET` that carries the client's credentials and the original
request in `X-Forwarded-Method`, `-Proto`, `-Host`, `-Uri` and `-For`: a 2xx lets the request through with the
configured response headers copied upstream, a 401, 403 or redirect is relayed to the client, anything else (and a timeout) refuses.
A field left null takes the preset's value (ForwardAuthPresets); ResolvedForwardAuth ForwardAuthPresets.Resolve(ForwardAuthConfig config) is the one
place that says which.

url.description: Absolute, or a path on the protected host (`/oauth2/start`).

returnParameter.description: The query parameter that carries the original URL (`rd`); null = `rd`.

ForwardAuthSignInConfig.description: A sign-in page a browser is redirected to, with the address it came from in a query parameter.

version.description: Concurrency version, incremented by the command pipeline on every change.

unknownHost.description: What a request for a name that no enabled host serves gets.

defaultCertificateId.description:
Certificate served when the SNI matches no host or is absent, and to hosts whose
            binding resolves to no certificate of their own. Null: such handshakes are rejected.

oneOf.description:
Null when it sets nothing (bool ConnectionSettings.SetsNothing): canonical JSON writes no key, so a
            stored revision keeps its bytes and its hash.

GlobalSettings.description: The global settings: one per document.

operation.description: What to do with the header.

value.description:
The value HeaderOperation.Set and HeaderOperation.Add send: 1-4096 visible
            ASCII characters, spaces or tabs, with no leading or trailing whitespace. Sent as written, with no placeholders. Absent for
            HeaderOperation.Remove.

request.description: Rules for the request the upstream receives, at most 32, one per header name; at most 32 also after the layers merge.

response.description: Rules for the response the client receives, at most 32, one per header name; at most 32 also after the layers merge.

HeadersSettings.description:
Custom headers: rules for the request the upstream receives and for the response the client receives. The layers merge
rule by rule, keyed on the header name (ignoring case) per direction: a layer's rule for a name replaces the rule a lower
layer has for it, and every other inherited rule stays. A route's rules go over its host's the same way.

HostTraffic.description: A host's traffic over the range.

enabled.description:
Send the header at all. Built-in default: off, so nothing is pinned on a browser's behalf until it is
            turned on.

maxAge.description:
Seconds a browser remembers the host as HTTPS-only (`max-age`), 0 to 63072000 (two years). Built-in
            default: one year (31536000). 0 is valid, and tells a browser that already remembers the host to forget it.

includeSubDomains.description:
Cover every subdomain too (`includeSubDomains`). Built-in default: off, because a subdomain that has
            no certificate of its own stops working over plain HTTP. A browser begins to trust the setting when it sees it, and
            keeps it for int? HstsSettings.MaxAge, so a wrong one is felt for as long as that.

preload.description:
Ask the browser vendors' preload lists to ship the host as HTTPS-only (`preload`). Built-in default:
            off. It needs bool? HstsSettings.IncludeSubDomains and a int? HstsSettings.MaxAge of at least a year, and it is hard to undo:
            browsers that ship the list keep refusing plain HTTP even after the header stops.

HstsSettings.description:
HTTP Strict Transport Security: the host's HTTPS responses tell a browser to keep the host on HTTPS for
int? HstsSettings.MaxAge seconds, and with bool? HstsSettings.IncludeSubDomains every subdomain too. Each field inherits on its
own. Paduraksa sends it only to HTTPS requests, and never for an IP literal or a loopback name.

certificateId.description: The certificate (allocated by a request); null when refused before one existed.

oneOf.description: The certificate's metadata after the attempt; null when there is none.

token.description: The full `pdk_...` string to present as a Bearer token. Not recoverable later.

IssuedApiToken.description: A newly issued token: the only time its secret is shown.

The JWS signature algorithms an ACME account key can use (RFC 8555 §6.2 requires a public-key algorithm and
forbids MACs and `none` for account keys). Persisted by the JOSE name (JwsAlgorithmNames), never by number.

The kind of key the vault generates for a certificate. Persisted by its stable name (VaultNames), never
by number. KeySpec.EcdsaP256 is the zero value and so the default.

LatencyFigures.description: Latency percentiles in milliseconds; all 0 when nothing was timed.

names.description: DNS names, `*.` wildcards and IP addresses; at least one.

keySpec.description: The kind of key the vault generates.

validity.description: How long it is valid from now (the vault caps it at the root's remaining validity); null for the default (90 days).

LocalCaLeafRequest.description: A new leaf certificate signed by the local CA.

reissued.description: How many were issued again from the current root.

failures.description: The ones that were not, with why (a name the new root's constraints don't permit, for one).

LocalCaReissueResult.description: What re-issuing the certificates a retiring root signed did.

keySpec.description: The kind of key the vault generates for the root.

validity.description: How long the root is valid from now; null for the default (ten years).

permittedDomains.description:
DNS domains to limit the root to: a name equal to one or under it. A device that trusts the root then accepts nothing for any
            other name. With no domains and no addresses the root is unlimited, which is the default.

permittedAddresses.description: IP addresses or CIDR networks to limit the root to.

LocalCaRequest.description: Creates the local CA root, if there is none. There is one local CA: asking again returns the existing root.

keySpec.description: The kind of key the vault generates for the new root.

validity.description: How long the new root is valid from now; null for the default (ten years).

permittedDomains.description: As on LocalCaRequest; the new root's own list, so add every domain it should issue for. None (and no addresses) makes the new root unlimited.

LocalCaRotateRequest.description:
Replaces the local CA root with a new one. Devices must trust the new root before what it signs works for them; what the old root signed
keeps working (and the old root stays downloadable) until it is retired.

oneOf.description: The root that signs; null before there is one.

LocalCaStatus.description: The local CA as it stands: the root that signs, what it is limited to, and the roots a rotation left behind.

name.description: The file's name inside the logs directory, e.g. `error.log` or `access-20261109T120000Z.log.gz`.

log.description: The log it belongs to: `access` or `error`.

lastModified.description: When it was last written, in UTC.

compressed.description: True for a rotated file that has been gzipped.

LogFileSummary.description:
One file in the logs directory: its name, which log it belongs to, its size, and when it was last written.
Served by the API's log list and shown by the dashboard's log page.

name.description: The file these lines come from.

log.description: The log it belongs to: `access` or `error`.

lines.description: The lines, oldest first, each at most 4096 characters.

truncated.description: True when the file (or the part that was read) held more than Lines carries.

LogFileTail.description:
The last lines of a log file, read without loading the whole file: at most 1000 lines out of the last 1 MiB (a rotated
file is decompressed up to a cap first), optionally only those matching a filter.

sequence.description: Position in the stream since the process started. A jump between two is what the reader skipped.

totalMs.description: Request start to the end of the response, in milliseconds.

clientAddress.description: The resolved client address (behind a trusted proxy, the one its header carried).

matchedHost.description: The configured host's first name, or absent when no host owned the request (a scanner, a typo, an address).

query.description: The query, `?` included, with sensitive parameters as `name=REDACTED`; absent when there is none or the file leaves it out.

status.description: The status sent, or absent when the gate dropped the connection without answering.

responseBytes.description: Response body bytes written to the client.

requestBytes.description: Request body bytes read from the client.

upstreamMs.description: The forward to the upstream, in milliseconds; absent when nothing was forwarded.

requestIdentifier.description: The `X-Request-Id` of the request: the one a trusted proxy sent, or Paduraksa's own.

cloudflareRay.description: `CF-Ray`, only when the request came through a trusted Cloudflare edge or tunnel.

LogTailEntry.description:
One request in the live access-log tail, as `access.log` would show it: the same caps, the same escaping of control
characters (`\xNN`) and the same redaction of sensitive query parameters. A request of a host whose access log is off is
never here.

username.description: The sign-in name (case does not matter).

LoginRequest.description: The first step of signing in.

enabled.description:
Serve the maintenance page. Built-in default: off. Not applied to an admin host (the config warns), so a layer
            that turns it on for every host can't lock the dashboard out.

status.description: The status of the answer: 503, 200, 500, 502, 504, 403, 404 or 410. Built-in default: 503.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Seconds a client is told to wait (`Retry-After`), 0 to 604800 (a week); 0 sends none. Built-in default: 0.

oneOf.description:
A named access list whose allowed addresses and countries reach the host as usual: a request the list's allow rules admit
skips the maintenance page. Only the address rules count (a password is never asked for here, and a list with no allow rule
bypasses nobody). Built-in default: none.

MaintenanceSettings.description:
A host that is down on purpose. While bool? MaintenanceSettings.Enabled, every request but the bypassed ones is answered with the
maintenance page and int? MaintenanceSettings.Status instead of reaching the upstream: after the host's access list, rules and HTTPS
redirect, so a refused client is still refused and plain HTTP still redirects, and after the managed `robots.txt`.
Each field inherits on its own.

requestsPerSecond.description: Requests answered a second, the connections the gate dropped included.

errorRate.description: The share of requests answered with a 5xx, 0 to 1.

refusedPerSecond.description: Requests the gate refused by a policy or a limit, a second.

bytesPerSecond.description: Response body bytes written to clients a second.

bytesInPerSecond.description: Request body bytes read from clients a second.

total.description: Time from the request's first byte to the end of the response.

upstream.description: Time spent forwarding and waiting for the upstream; the difference to Total is the proxy's own.

range.description: How far back Series and the tables reach.

bucketWidth.description: The usual width of one Series step; see int MetricsSeriesPoint.WidthSeconds for each step's own.

series.description:
The chart, oldest first, from the first step the server observed to the last: every step in between is there, and one the server
was not running for has int MetricsSeriesPoint.CoveredSeconds 0 (no data), so downtime is a gap and not a line through it.

hosts.description: The busiest hosts over the range, most requests first.

upstreams.description: The upstreams that were forwarded to over the range, most errors first.

MetricsOverview.description:
The overview page's data: the pace now, a chart over the range, the busiest hosts and the upstreams' errors. Read from the
sampler's memory (and the last hour of rollups it started from) for the hour and from the persisted one-minute rollups for longer.

MetricsRange.description: How far back the overview looks. The hour comes from the sampler's memory, the rest from the one-minute rollups.

requestsPerSecond.description: Requests answered a second over the seconds that were observed, not the step's whole width.

errorsPerSecond.description: 5xx answers a second, over the observed seconds.

refusedPerSecond.description: Requests the gate refused by a policy or a limit, a second over the observed seconds.

total.description: Latency percentiles of the requests answered in the step.

upstream.description: Upstream time percentiles of the requests forwarded in the step.

widthSeconds.description: How long the step is. Usually TimeSpan MetricsOverview.BucketWidth; the hour's steps from before the server started are a minute wide (the one it started in is cut short where the ten-second steps begin).

coveredSeconds.description: How many of those seconds the server was running to count them; less than the width for a step the server started or stopped in, and 0 for no data.

MetricsSeriesPoint.description:
One step of the chart: the figures over the WidthSeconds starting at Start. A step whose
CoveredSeconds is 0 has no data: Paduraksa was not running (every figure is 0, and a chart should break its
line there rather than draw a zero). A step that was covered and saw no requests has a rate of 0 and no latency (0).

stripPrefix.description:
Take the route's path off the front. A request that spells the prefix differently from the
            route (encoded, with `//`, `;` or dot segments) can't be stripped without guessing, and gets 404. Not on a route
            whose path is `/`.

addPrefix.description:
Put this in front of what is forwarded: starts with `/`, no trailing `/`, at most 256
            characters of a URL path (letters, digits, `-._~!$&'()*+,;=:@/` and percent escapes), with no empty or dot
            segments. Sent as written.

rewriteLocation.description:
With StripPrefix: give an upstream's `Location` the client's prefix back
            (`/login` becomes `/app/login`; one that already starts with `/app` is left alone). Null is on; turn it off for an
            upstream that redirects to other routes of the host, which the mapping would put under this one. Only with a strip.

PathRewriteConfig.description:
The path a route forwards: the client's, with the route's own path taken off the front, a fixed prefix put on, or both
(`/app/x` becomes `/x`, or `/api/x`). It works on the path as the client sent it, without decoding or
re-encoding it, and the query is untouched. With bool PathRewriteConfig.StripPrefix the upstream is told the stripped prefix in
`X-Forwarded-Prefix`, and a `Location` it answers with that points into its own paths gets the client's
prefix back.

verifyRejected.description: Answers to the verify endpoint that were refused: a bad challenge or solution.

blockedNonBrowser.description: Requests refused with 403 for having no token and not coming from a browser.

tokensRejected.description: Cookies that were not accepted, by reason.

difficulty.description: Leading zero bits a solution needs (a route can't change it).

routeOverrides.description: Routes whose switch differs from the host's: exempt when the host is on, protected when it is off.

difficulty.description:
Leading zero bits of SHA-256 a solution needs, 8 to 28. Built-in default: 16, well under a second on an
            ordinary laptop.

tokenLifetimeHours.description: How long the cookie lasts, in hours, 1 to 720. Built-in default: 168 (seven days).

ProofOfWorkSettings.description:
The browser check: a visitor without a valid token gets a small page that solves a SHA-256 proof of work, then a
signed, expiring cookie bound to this host and client address lets it through. Each field inherits on its own.

generation.description: The live snapshot generation, when PublishOutcomeStatus.Published.

errors.description: Why it failed, if it did.

revision.description: The revision whose publish this is: the committed one, or the newer one that superseded it.

PublishOutcome.description:
How the snapshot publish after a commit went. The publisher only publishes the latest snapshot:
when a newer revision is queued before this one went live, this one is superseded, and its outcome is that of the
publish that carries it (Revision then names the newer revision).

PublishOutcomeStatus.description: The publisher's verdict on a committed revision's snapshot.

oneOf.description: The policy those routes apply; absent when they are not limited.

RateLimitOverride.description: Routes that apply another rate-limit policy, or none.

id.description: Identity; the first half of a bucket's stable slot identity.

requests.description:
Whole requests per Per, at least 1. The token rate is this over the
            period's seconds.

per.description: The period the rate is measured over.

burst.description:
The bucket's size in tokens, at least 1: how many requests may arrive at once before the rate
            has to earn more.

key.description: What one bucket belongs to: a client IP, an IP and path, or a header value.

header.description:
With RateLimitKey.Header: the request header whose value is the partition key.
            Required exactly then, and a valid header name (a token).

RateLimitPolicyConfig.description:
A named token bucket that hosts and routes apply: int RateLimitPolicyConfig.Requests per RateLimitPeriod RateLimitPolicyConfig.Per seconds, with a
bucket of int RateLimitPolicyConfig.Burst tokens, keyed the way RateLimitKey RateLimitPolicyConfig.Key says. It is a top-level object, so two hosts
can name one policy and still keep their own buckets (docs/design/config.md "State that survives a publish").

RateLimitPolicyId.description: A rate-limit policy: one token bucket's rate, burst and partition key, which hosts and routes name.

overrides.description: The routes that differ from the host's policy, grouped by what they apply instead.

oneOf.description: The policy the host applies; absent when it names none.

enabled.description: Apply the resolved policy. Built-in default: on. Off turns an inherited policy off.

oneOf.description:
The policy to apply; null = inherit. With bool? RateLimitSettings.Enabled off the reference is kept but inert, so
            turning the switch back on needs no second lookup.

RateLimitSettings.description:
Which rate-limit policy a layer applies. RateLimitPolicyId? RateLimitSettings.PolicyId names a policy the document declares; it inherits
field by field, so a host can turn an inherited policy off without forgetting which one it was, and a route can
inherit its host's, name another, or turn it off. A layer that names a policy without stating
bool? RateLimitSettings.Enabled leaves the switch to the built-in default, which is on: naming a policy is the whole job.

RecoveryCodes.description: Recovery codes, shown once: only their hashes are kept.

target.description:
Absolute `http`/`https` URL in printable ASCII (punycode host, percent-encoded path);
            it becomes the `Location` header.

preservePath.description:
Append the request's path and query to Target (which then has no
            query or fragment).

accessList.description: An access list refused them by address, country or password.

rateLimit.description: A rate limit turned them away.

proofOfWork.description: The proof-of-work page, or a refusal of its token.

signIn.description: An auth provider refused, redirected or failed.

requestLimits.description: Over a request target, header or body limit (413, 414, 431).

connection.description: The connection could not serve the host: a 421, the origin lockdown or a missing client certificate.

other.description: A policy with no kind of its own.

unknown.description: Refusals stored before the reasons were kept: counted, but of an unknown reason.

noRoute.description: The host has no route for the path.

unavailable.description: The 503 of no live config or no endpoint.

dropped.description: The connection was dropped without an answer.

refused.description: Everything refused: the first nine reasons.

RefusalReasons.description: Requests the gate turned away, by reason. The first nine are the refusals the overview counts as refused; the last four are answers the gate gave without a policy.

coveredSeconds.description: How many of its seconds the server observed; 0 is a time it was not running, not a step with no refusals.

refused.description: What was refused in it, by reason (counts, not rates).

RefusalStep.description: One step of the refusals over time.

keySpec.description: The new key's kind; null keeps the current kind.

validity.description: How long the new certificate is valid from now; null for the default of its source.

ReissueRequest.description:
Re-issues a self-signed or local-CA certificate under the same CertificateId and a new key: its names
stay, and Specific bindings survive.

maxBodySize.description:
Largest request body in bytes; 0 is no limit. Built-in default: 100 MiB. Over it is 413: at once when the request declares
            its size, mid-upload when it doesn't. A route may set its own.

maxHeaderCount.description: Most header lines a request may carry, 8 to 128. Built-in default: 100. Host-wide: a route can't set it.

maxHeaderBytes.description:
Most bytes the header names and values may take together, 1 KiB to 64 KiB. Built-in default: 32 KiB.
            Host-wide: a route can't set it.

maxUrlLength.description:
Longest request target (path and query, as sent), in bytes, 256 to 16 KiB. Built-in default: 8 KiB. Host-wide:
            a route can't set it.

RequestLimitsSettings.description:
How much of a request a host takes. Each field inherits on its own. A request over a limit is refused before the upstream
sees it: 413 for the body, 431 for the headers, 414 for the request target. Sizes are bytes.

contentType.description: The `Content-Type` header: visible ASCII, spaces and tabs.

leaves.description: How many certificates it signed that are still in use; the root can be retired when this is 0.

changes.description: What it changed against its parent.

document.description: The config as of this revision, versions included.

RevisionDetail.description: A revision with what it changed and its whole document.

changes.description: The structural diff, as a dry run reports it.

RevisionDiff.description: What changed from one revision to another.

RevisionRef.description: A committed revision, by ID and display number.

documentSha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical document, lowercase hex.

parentId.description: The revision it was made on top of; null for the first.

message.description: The optional note.

oneOf.description: Passthrough, a preset, or the operator's text. Built-in default: passthrough.

customText.description:
The text RobotsMode.Custom serves. Set with that mode at its layer, or inherited from one that set it;
any other mode ignores it. Line endings are normalised when the proxy compiles it, not in the stored document.

RobotsSettings.description:
What the host answers at `/robots.txt`. There is no route-level override: a host has one file, and every route
shares it. Each field inherits on its own, so a layer can change the mode and keep the text below it.

RotateDnsCredentialBody.description: Replaces a DNS provider's credential, keeping the provider (and everything that uses it).

order.description:
A specificity tiebreaker: lower runs first between routes of equal match kind and path length;
            equal orders keep their listed order.

path.description:
Starts with `/`; decoded and canonical (no `\`, `//`, `;`, dot segments,
            percent-encoding, query or fragment). Matching ignores case, but the path keeps the case it was written in; two
            routes of a host with the same match kind can't have paths that differ only in case.

oneOf.description: How the path the upstream receives differs from the client's; null forwards it as received.

RouteConfig.description: One route of a proxy host.

RouteId.description: A route of a proxy host.

oneOf.description:
The route-level subset of ProofOfWorkSettings: only bool? ProofOfWorkSettings.Enabled is
accepted here. It overrides the host's resolved switch either way, so one path can be exempt or protected.

The route-level subset of RateLimitSettings: only bool? RateLimitSettings.Enabled and
RateLimitPolicyId? RateLimitSettings.PolicyId are accepted here, field by field over the host's resolved values. So a
route can inherit its host's policy, name another one, or turn the limit off for its own paths.

Field by field over the host's resolved list: a route inherits the host's, names another, or turns the list
            off for its own paths.

The route-level subset of RequestLimitsSettings: only long? RequestLimitsSettings.MaxBodySize is
accepted here, over the host's resolved value, so an upload route can take more (or less) than the rest of the host.
The header and URL limits are judged before a route is known, so they belong to the host.

Field by field over the host's resolved set: a route inherits the host's, names another, or turns the rules off
            for its own paths.

Field by field over the host's resolved provider: a route inherits the host's, names another, or turns authentication off
            for its own paths (the route that serves the provider's sign-in pages has to).
Rule by rule over the host's resolved rules: a route's rule for a header name replaces the host's for it.

RouteSettings.description:
The route layer: the route-level subset of HostSettings, on top of the host's resolved
            settings. Null fields inherit from the host.

RuleAction.description: What a rule set does with a request its rule matches.

action.description: What happens to a request the rule matches.

RuleConfig.description: One rule: every condition in RuleMatchConfig RuleConfig.Match must hold for it to apply.

oneOf.description: The path pattern.

methods.description: HTTP methods, upper case (canonical order: sorted, no duplicates); null = any.

oneOf.description: The user-agent condition.

RuleMatchConfig.description: The conditions of a rule; one that is left out isn't tested.

pattern.description:
Exact, prefix and glob start with `/` and are written decoded, in the canonical form a route's
            path takes. A regex is matched without backtracking against the canonical path, ignoring case.

RulePathConfig.description: A path condition: how to read Pattern and the pattern itself.

RulePathKind.description: How a rule's path condition reads its pattern. All four compare the canonical matching path ignoring ASCII case.

id.description: Identity. The built-in presets (RuleSetPresets) have reserved IDs and are never part of a document.

RuleSetConfig.description:
A named, ordered list of request rules that hosts and routes apply: each rule names a path, methods and a user agent a
request must all match, and what to do with one that does. The first rule that matches decides; a request no rule matches
goes on through the rest of the chain. It is a top-level object, so one set can guard several hosts and routes.

RuleSetId.description:
A rule set: an ordered list of path, method and user-agent rules, which hosts and routes name. The built-in presets
            have reserved IDs.

oneOf.description: The set those routes apply; absent when they apply none.

RuleSetOverride.description: Routes that apply another rule set, or none.

overrides.description: The routes that differ from the host's set, grouped by what applies to them instead.

oneOf.description: The set the host names; absent when it names none.

builtIn.description: It is one of the built-in presets, which have no page of their own to open.

denied.description: Requests a rule refused with 403 over the range, across every host that applies the set.

dropped.description: Requests a rule dropped without an answer.

allowed.description: Requests an allow rule took out of the set's later rules.

timeouts.description: Regex matches that ran past their timeout and were decided by the rule's action (a deny or drop counts as a match, an allow as none); 0 in a healthy proxy.

RuleSetRef.description: A named rule set with what it has done since the process started, across every host and route that applies it.

enabled.description: Apply the resolved set. Built-in default: on. Off lifts an inherited set.

oneOf.description: The set to apply; null = inherit. With bool? RuleSetSettings.Enabled off the reference is kept but inert.

RuleSetSettings.description:
Which rule set a layer applies. RuleSetId? RuleSetSettings.RuleSetId names a set the document declares or a built-in preset;
            both fields inherit on their own, so a host can turn an inherited set off without forgetting which one it was, and a route
            can inherit its host's, name another, or turn it off. A layer that names a set without stating bool? RuleSetSettings.Enabled
            leaves the switch to the built-in default, which is on. One set per layer: several concerns are several rules in one set.

empty.description: Also match a missing or empty user agent.

RuleUserAgentConfig.description:
A user-agent condition: it holds when the header contains any of Contains, or when
            Empty is set and the request has no user agent or an empty one.

code.description: The six digits from the authenticator.

SecondFactorRequest.description: The second step: exactly one of a TOTP code or a recovery code.

range.description: How far back the counters reach: the hour is the sampler's memory (and the hour before a restart), the rest the one-minute rollups.

proofOfWork.description: The proof-of-work gate's counters over the range.

rateLimit.description: The rate limiter's counters over the range.

accessLists.description: The access lists' counters over the range.

hosts.description: The enabled hosts, by name, with what each refused over the range.

forwardAuth.description: Every auth provider's counters over the range, summed, a deleted provider's included.

connections.description: The connection stage: its limit and deny list as configured now, what it refused over the range, and what it counts now.

refusals.description: What the gate refused over the range, by reason.

series.description: The refusals by reason over time, one step per Step (the hour mixes minutes from before a restart with ten-second steps): every step from the first the server observed to the last, a step with `coveredSeconds` 0 being a time it was not running.

step.description: The width of a step of Series.

from.description: The first moment inside the range the server observed: the counters cover from here to SampledAt, less any time it was down. Absent when it observed none of the range.

SecurityOverview.description:
What protects the hosts and how much work it has done: the gate's counters over a range, kept in the metrics' rollups so a restart
doesn't reset them, the refusals by reason and over time, and each enabled host's protections as the live snapshot compiled them.

names.description: DNS names, `*.` wildcards and IP addresses; at least one. The first is the common name when it is a DNS name of at most 64 characters.

keySpec.description: The kind of key the vault generates, on the wire its stable name (`ecdsa-p256`, `ecdsa-p384`, `rsa-2048`, `rsa-3072`, `rsa-4096`).

validity.description: How long it is valid from now (at most 825 days); null for the default (one year).

SelfSignedCertificateRequest.description: A new self-signed certificate. Public data only: the key is made in the vault and never appears here.

oneOf.description:
Which header wins. Built-in default: ServerHeaderMode.Paduraksa, the name without a
            version.

value.description:
The header ServerHeaderMode.Custom sends: 1-128 visible ASCII characters or spaces, with no
            leading or trailing space. Required once the resolved mode is ServerHeaderMode.Custom; ignored by
            every other mode.

ServerHeaderSettings.description:
What the host's responses say in `Server`. ServerHeaderMode? ServerHeaderSettings.Mode and string? ServerHeaderSettings.Value inherit on
their own, like every other nested setting.

SessionId.description:
An admin session. UuidV4: a session's ID is shown in the session list and handed to the dashboard, so it
should not tell when the session began. It is a handle, not a credential: the cookie value is the credential, a
separate 256-bit random value of which only the hash is stored.

sessionId.description: The session (a handle, not the cookie).

secondFactorRequired.description: The password was right but a second factor is owed: only `auth/second-factor` accepts this session until it is given.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends (when the partial session ends, if a second factor is owed).

SessionStarted.description: A session that was just started, by signing in or by setup. Its cookie travels in `Set-Cookie` only, never in a body.

id.description: The session (a handle, not the cookie).

lastSeenAt.description: When it was last used (to within the touch interval).

expiresAt.description: Its absolute end; it ends earlier if idle too long.

secondFactorCompleted.description: False for a session still waiting for the second factor.

current.description: The session that asked for the list.

SessionSummary.description: An active session, for the session list.

oneOf.description: The session the response sets a cookie for; null only if signing the new Owner in failed, in which case they sign in as usual.

SetupCompleted.description: The result of first-run setup: the new Owner, signed in.

setupToken.description: The one-time token from the server log or `paduraksa setup-token`.

displayName.description: Shown in the UI; the username when null or empty.

SetupStatus.description: Whether the first Owner exists. Until it does, the admin app serves only the setup flow.

allowed.description: Requests a provider let through, from its answer or from its decision cache.

denied.description: Requests a provider refused (a relayed 401, 403 or 407).

redirected.description: Requests sent to a sign-in page.

cacheHits.description: Allows answered from the decision cache, with no call.

calls.description: Calls made to the providers' endpoints.

errors.description: Calls that failed or got an answer the proxy refuses to act on (502).

timeouts.description: Calls that ran out of time (504).

busy.description: Requests refused with 503 because too many calls were already running.

SignInCounters.description: The auth providers' counters, summed over every provider the live config names.

request.description: The request to ask "what would this get, and why" about.

oneOf.description: The config to simulate against; null for the live one.

SimulateBody.description: The body of `POST /api/v1/simulate`: which config to run the request against, and the request.

health.description: Its health in the live proxy: health is live state, so for a draft or revision it is the live proxy's answer for the destination with the same ID.

SimulationDestination.description: A destination of the route's upstream, as the target config lists it.

custom.description: An operator's page. False: the page built into Paduraksa.

source.description: Which layer the operator's page came from (the global defaults, the profile, the host); built-in when it isn't one.

mode.description: A message in the built-in layout, or the operator's own document.

SimulationErrorPage.description: Which page an answer is served as, to a client that accepts HTML (anything else gets plain text).

SimulationHealth.description: What is known about a destination's health.

summary.description: Why, in one line: the step that decided.

statusCode.description: The status, when the gate answers.

location.description: The `Location` of a redirect, built as the real response builds it.

body.description: The body of a short text answer.

oneOf.description:
The page a browser is served when the answer is one of the proxy's own error pages; absent for a redirect, a
            forward, a drop and an answer that is only text (a Respond host's).

SimulationOutcomeKind.description: What the gate does with the request.

url.description:
The absolute `http` or `https` URL: scheme, host, port, path and query. The `Host`
            header is its authority, unless Headers sets one.

clientIp.description:
The client's address (IPv4 or IPv6). Behind a proxy (Arrival), the address the
            proxy reports.

method.description: Default `GET`. Case matters, as on the wire: `get` is not `GET`.

arrival.description: How the request reaches Paduraksa. Default: directly.

peerIp.description:
The connection-level peer, for a request that comes through a proxy (Arrival other
            than direct) or with ProxyProtocol. Default: an address the config trusts as that kind of proxy
            (loopback when it trusts none). A direct request's peer is the client, so setting it there is refused.

proxyProtocol.description:
A PROXY protocol header arrived first: PeerIp is the address it carried.
            The listener must expect one: otherwise the connection is rejected, as the real one would be.

transportIp.description:
With ProxyProtocol only: the socket's remote address (the load balancer; it must
            be one of the listener's trusted sources). Default: loopback.

oneOf.description:
The TLS context; `https` URLs only (a plain-HTTP listener speaks HTTP/1.1 and has no handshake).
            Default: SNI from the URL, HTTP/2, TLS 1.3.

country.description:
The country Cloudflare would report for the client (`CF-IPCountry`): a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code, `T1`
            for Tor or `XX` for unknown. Only a request that arrives through Cloudflare (Arrival) carries it; to see
            the gate ignore one a client forged, send a `CF-IPCountry` header on another arrival. Default: no header, so the country is unknown.

SimulationRequest.description:
A request to ask "what would this get, and why" about. A URL and a client IP are enough; everything else
defaults to a plain GET from a client that connects directly.

oneOf.description: The verdict; set exactly when Status is SimulationStatus.Simulated.
The route's upstream, when the outcome forwards.

SimulationResult.description:
The answer to "what would this request get, and why": the outcome and the ordered trace of what the real
gate did, or, when there was nothing to simulate against, why not.

revision.description:
The revision the config is (the live one's, or the stored revision); null for a draft, and for the
            live config before the first commit.

summary.description: One line saying it in words.

host.description: The host it concerns, once one matched.

route.description: The route it concerns, once one matched.

policyIndex.description: Policy steps: the policy's position in its chain, from 0.

SimulationStepKind.description: Which gate step a SimulationStep is, in the order they run.

SimulationStepVerdict.description: What a step did to the request.

SimulationTarget.description:
The config to simulate against: the live snapshot, a stored revision, or a draft (a document or a pending command)
that is validated and compiled but never stored or published.

SimulationTargetDraftCommandSimulationTa.description:
A pending command, applied to the current config and validated and compiled as its dry run would. Whatever
            bool ConfigCommand.DryRun says, nothing is stored or published.

SimulationTargetDraftDocumentSimulationT.description: A whole document. Validated and compiled like an import; its versions are not looked at.

SimulationTargetKind.description: Which config the simulator runs the request against.

serverName.description:
The name in the ClientHello. Default: the URL's host when it is a DNS name; none for an IP
            address. Set it to test a connection negotiated for one name that then asks for another (the 421 case).

SimulationTls.description: The TLS context of an HTTPS request. Every part defaults to what a browser would do for the URL.

destinations.description: The upstream's destinations in the target config, with their live health.

loadBalancing.description: The YARP load-balancing policy; null for YARP's default.

SimulationUpstream.description: The upstream the request is forwarded to. Load balancing is random: no destination is named as the one chosen.

oneOf.description: Lowest TLS version over TCP (QUIC is always 1.3). Built-in default: TLS 1.2.
ALPN offered over TCP. Built-in default: HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1.

http3.description: Serve over HTTP/3 when the listener exists. Built-in default: on.

TlsSettings.description: TLS settings; each field inherits on its own. A layer that sets none is the same as no layer.

malformed.description: Not a token this build issues.

badTag.description: Altered, or issued for another host or client address.

tooEasy.description: Valid, but easier than the host's current difficulty.

TokenRejections.description: Why proof-of-work cookies were not accepted.

TotpConfirmation.description: A code from the authenticator, to confirm an enrolment.

provisioningUri.description: The `otpauth://` URI for the QR code: shown once, not stored.

TotpEnrollmentStarted.description: The start of a TOTP enrolment.

mode.description: How the client IP reaches us.

header.description:
Generic mode only: the header carrying the client; null = `X-Forwarded-For`, read right
            to left.

useTrueClientIp.description:
Cloudflare modes: also accept `True-Client-IP` when `CF-Connecting-IP` is
            absent.

forwardedForFallback.description:
Cloudflare modes: fall back to the right-most untrusted `X-Forwarded-For`
            entry.

trustForwardedProto.description:
Generic mode only: take the request scheme from the trusted proxies'
            `X-Forwarded-Proto`.

TrustedProxySettings.description:
Trusted proxies in front of Paduraksa. Only a peer inside the trusted set may supply the
client IP through a header; anyone else is the client.

roles.description: The complete new set of roles (not a delta); at least one when given.

disabled.description: True disables the user (ending their sessions; their tokens stop working), false re-enables them and clears a lockout.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Changes a user; a null member stays as it is.

UploadForm.description: The upload form, for the API description only.

id.description: Identity; also the YARP cluster ID.

loadBalancing.description:
Null: whatever YARP's default is (today power of two choices); a value pins the
            policy, so null and LoadBalancingPolicy.PowerOfTwoChoices are kept apart.

oneOf.description: Passive health (transport failure rate); null = off.
Active health probes; null = off.

maxConnectionsPerServer.description: Null: no limit beyond the HTTP client's default.

oneOf.description: How HTTPS destinations are authenticated; null = the system trust store.
The `Host` the upstream receives; null = the client's own (UpstreamHostHeaderMode.Original).
Connect and idle timeouts; null = the built-in defaults.

UpstreamConfig.description: An upstream: a set of destinations that routes proxy to, compiled into a YARP cluster.

UpstreamHealthState.description: Whether and how an upstream is serving, as the live proxy sees it.

oneOf.description: The latest change of the upstream or any of its destinations since the process started; null if none.

value.description:
With UpstreamHostHeaderMode.Custom: a host name or IP address, with a port when the
            upstream's virtual host needs one (`app.internal`, `app.internal:8080`, `[::1]:8080`). Absent otherwise.

UpstreamHostHeaderConfig.description:
The `Host` header an upstream receives. SNI follows it on an HTTPS destination, so the certificate is asked for
            and checked against the name sent (a pinned fingerprint is not tied to any name).

UpstreamId.description: An upstream, compiled into a YARP cluster.

connect.description: TCP and TLS connect to a destination, 100 ms to 5 minutes; null = 10 seconds.

idle.description: How long a request, a response stream or an upgraded connection (a WebSocket) may go with no data in either direction before the proxy closes it, 1 second to 24 hours; zero = never; null = 1 hour.

UpstreamTimeoutsConfig.description: How long the proxy waits on an upstream. Each value left null is the built-in default.

pinnedSha256.description:
With UpstreamTlsTrust.Pinned: the SHA-256 fingerprints of the certificates to
            accept, 64 hex digits each (colons allowed, as `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256` prints them).

UpstreamTlsConfig.description: How the proxy authenticates an upstream's HTTPS destinations.

errors.description: Forwards that failed on its side: a refused or timed-out connection, a broken response, no destination to try.

p95Ms.description: The 95th-percentile upstream time, as double HostTraffic.P95Ms.

UpstreamTraffic.description: An upstream's forwards over the range.

UserId.description: An admin user; its entity is `UserRow` in Data.

username.description: The sign-in name, as the user typed it when created.

displayName.description: The name shown in the UI.

roles.description: The roles the user holds, in a fixed order.

twoFactorEnabled.description: An authenticator is enrolled, so signing in needs a code.

disabled.description: The user cannot sign in, and their tokens and sessions are dead.

locked.description: Sign-in is refused for now after too many failures.

updatedAt.description: When the user was last changed.

UserSummary.description: An admin user as the admin surfaces see them.

api.description: The API's major version, as in its path prefix: `v1`.

commit.description: The full SHA of the commit the build came from; null for a build that was not given one (the container image build passes it as `-p:SourceRevisionId`). Always written.

VersionInfo.description: What is running: the product's version and the commit it was built from.

bearer.description: An API token issued to a user. A signed-in session cookie is accepted as well.
